summary.title: For Engineers - PagerDuty Security Training
summary.one_liner: An open-source, transcribed engineering security training covering SQL injection (with prepared statements as the fix) and secure password storage using hashing, salts and peppers.
keywords: what is sql injection in plain english
takeaways: SQL injection happens when user input changes the structure of a query at runtime; users should only supply values, never alter the SQL.
Blacklists of bad keywords and manual escaping of quotes are unreliable defenses; prepared statements with bound placeholders are the surefire fix.
Blind SQL injection (boolean-based and time-based) can still extract data when results are not shown directly.
Passwords should be stored as salted hashes: salts are unique per password and public, while a pepper is a secret kept outside the database.
Fast hashes can be brute-forced in real time once stolen, so password storage needs slow hashing as well (the page ends before fully covering this).
summary.summary: This page is the open-source web version of PagerDuty's internal "Security Training for Engineers" (April 2018), presented as a transcribed talk with slide-by-slide commentary. The portion captured covers framework security assumptions, Hackday security rules, and a redacted story of a responsibly disclosed bug. The main technical content is SQL injection: a login-page example, UNION and blind (boolean and time-based) techniques, why blacklists and escaping fail, and how prepared statements separate query structure from values. The text then moves to password storage, explaining hashing, rainbow tables, salts, and peppers, and ends mid-argument about why slow hashing is needed. Reading references to OWASP and pentestmonkey cheat sheets are included.
